title: The product of two finite complex partial sums equals the diagonal-grouped convolution plus a corner term, which the naive Cauchy identity omits
statement: For f, g : Nat -> Complex and any n, with F i j := f i * g j: (sum_{i<n} f i) * (sum_{j<n} g j) ~ TRIANGLE(F,n) + CORNER(F,n), where TRIANGLE is the antidiagonal sum sum_{k<n} sum_{i<=k} F i (k-i) and CORNER is sum_{i<n} sum_{j<i} F i ((n-i)+j), the sum over {(i,j) : i<n, j<n, i+j>=n}. Equivalence is Complex.Equiv, a DEFINED Prop relation on a setoid, never Eq. THIS EXISTS BECAUSE THE NAIVE FINITE CAUCHY IDENTITY IS FALSE. The claim (sum a)(sum b) = sum_{k<n} sum_{i<=k} a_i * b_{k-i} was dispatched as a target and REFUTED by hand at n = 2: the left side contains a_1*b_1 and the right, being only the antidiagonal triangle, does not. This theorem is not a weaker replacement -- it names and quantifies the exact defect, and the CORNER at n = 2 is exactly the missing a_1*b_1. A NOTE ON `AxNat`, which appears throughout the formal statement: the `Ax` is `axeyum`, not `axiom`. `lean_pp` roots the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive naturals there only so exported terms do not shadow Lean's own `Nat`. It collides badly with `AxReal`, where `Ax` DOES mean axiomatized and the trusted surface is 30. Every prelude involved here -- nat, rat, creal, complex -- measures 0.

formal.statement: ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Complex)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Complex)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Complex.Equiv (Complex.mul (Complex.sumRange x0 x2) (Complex.sumRange x1 x2)) (Complex.add (Complex.sumRange (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Complex.sumRange (fun (x4 : AxNat) => (fun (x5 : AxNat) => fun (x6 : AxNat) => Complex.mul (x0 x5) (x1 x6)) x4 (AxNat.sub x3 x4)) (AxNat.succ x3)) x2) (Complex.sumRange (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Complex.sumRange (fun (x4 : AxNat) => (fun (x5 : AxNat) => (fun (x6 : AxNat) => fun (x7 : AxNat) => Complex.mul (x0 x6) (x1 x7)) x3 x5) (AxNat.add (AxNat.sub x2 x3) x4)) x3) x2)))))

evidence.supports: `Complex.sumRange_mul_eq_diag_add_corner` is admitted with exactly the type in formal.statement. It composes `Complex.sumRange_mul_double[f,g,n,n]` -- which turns a product of partial sums into the RECTANGLE sum over {(i,j) : i<n, j<n} -- with `Complex.sumRange_rect_eq_diag_add_corner`, via Equiv.trans. The rectangle decomposition is itself the Equiv-port of Nat.sumRange_rect_eq_diag_add_corner, same induction structure. THE PORT IS NOT MECHANICAL: Complex.Equiv has no free single-sided congruence, so every rewrite under `add` needs an explicit add_congr paired with Equiv.refl on the untouched side, where over Nat it is just Eq and a rewrite chain.

prior_art.attribution: standard attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source. Cauchy's theorem concerns INFINITE series under absolute convergence. The finite-partial-sum statement proved here is the elementary index-set decomposition underneath it, and the corner term is exactly what vanishes in the limit under Cauchy's hypotheses.

notes:
WHAT IS NOT PROVED, stated so it is not inferred: Mertens' theorem, or any statement that the corner term VANISHES in the limit. That is the analytic content of the Cauchy product and it needs absolute convergence and an estimate on the corner, neither of which is here. This is the finite, purely combinatorial identity.

A CONSTRUCTION DETAIL WORTH RECORDING because it is the failure mode this kernel keeps hitting: the two `rectangle(F,n)` terms arrive in beta-equivalent but syntactically DIFFERENT shapes (an un-curried double_fn versus F applied through curried helpers), so the composition leans on the kernel's own beta-reduction under nested binders during type-checking. That is the same class of reliance diagonal_step_c already places on iota-reduction. It type-checked cleanly, but a term merely beta-equivalent to what a lemma expects is the shape that produces this family's ~180 s rejections.

The proof is constructive throughout: no Classical.em, no propext, no funext, no Quot.sound.

external_status is `proved`: elementary classical combinatorics, formalized. What is locally notable is the direction of travel -- the claim entered the queue FALSE, a lane refuted it by hand rather than proving something adjacent under the briefed name, and the repair is what got recorded, over Nat first and then here.
